backtest.scope: Out of sample. Walk-forward back-test of every closed public_records_litigation matter, each modeled only from matters that closed before it opened, with the change check and the band adjustment also run as of that day. Matched on matter type only (not this proposal's selection rules), minimum 8 comps.
backtest.headline: Overruns at P75 and P90 are within what chance would explain at n=53.
backtest.verdict: Overruns at P75 and P90 are within what chance would explain at n=53. At the planning P75, 13 of 53 back-tested matters cost more; the band implies about 13. At the planning P90, 4 of 53 back-tested matters cost more; the band implies about 5.

assumptions.text: Comps with a hearing (n=24) had a median cost of $86,000, 2.3x the median of comps without one ($36,700, n=19). Quote the hearing as a separate phase, or state that it is excluded.
The 11 comps above the P75 cost $133,100 more on average than the other 32. Hearing accounts for 66% of that gap ($87,300). Set a scope limit or a separate fee for that phase.
Comps with more than 2 parties (n=17) had a median cost of $86,600, 1.7x the median of the rest ($51,400, n=26). State the number of parties the fee covers and price extra ones separately.

11 matters of this type closed abnormally (settled early, transferred or other) and are not in the comps. The figures assume the matter runs to completion; say what happens to the fee if it ends early.
The phase split for 7 of 43 comps comes from the date-window fallback, not task codes. Treat per-phase figures as lower confidence; totals are not affected.

Across the 43 comps, 3.9% of worked value was written down before billing and 3.1% of invoiced fees was not collected. A fee built from billed amounts would understate the work; the figures here use worked hours.

warnings: Heavily skewed (n=43): the P90 is 2.8x the median and the mean is 1.3x the median. A few expensive matters dominate; an average would mislead.
